So applying retro template to product yields precursors: left side is product pattern? Actually retro_smarts_template: product side on left? Usually retro template is product -> reactants, so left side is product pattern, right side is reactants. Here left side: [C:7]-[#8:6]-[c:5]1... which looks like a phenyl attached via O to C (maybe a carbonyl?). Right side: O=[N+...]... which is sulfonyl aryl? Wait right side includes O=[N+...]...-c... which looks like sulfonyl aryl. That seems like product is aryl sulfonamide? Actually right side includes O=[N+...]... which is nitro? No O=[N+;H0;D3:1](-[O-]) is nitro group. So right side is nitro aryl? Hmm.

But we have mapped_rxn showing full reaction: product >> precursors? The mapped_rxn appears to have product on left? It shows ...>>... The arrow direction: left side is product? The mapped_rxn: 'O=[N+:15]([O-])[c:14]1...>>[CH3:1][C:2]...' So left side is nitro aryl? Right side is complex molecule (the product). So the mapped_rxn is forward reaction (reactants -> product). So retro direction would be product -> reactants, which matches retro_smarts_template left side is product pattern? Actually left side of retro_smarts_template is [C:7]-[#8:6]-[c:5]... which is part of product (the phenoxy). Right side is nitro aryl. So applying retro template to product will give nitro aryl as one precursor and something else? Let's just use apply_template tool with target molecule SMILES (product) and template ID "2895". Let's convert to SMILES: CH3 C(CH3)(CH3) O C(=O) N1CCN( aromatic )CC1. The aromatic part: c2c(c3c2OC2(CCC2)CC3) with NH2 substituent. So product SMILES likely: CC(C)(C)OC(=O)N1CCN(c2cc(N)cc3c2OC2(CCC2)CC3)CC1. That's exactly precursor1 earlier. Wait that's the same as precursor1. So product is that? Actually precursor1 is that. So maybe product is sulfonamide linking that to nitro phenyl? But mapped_rxn left side is nitro aryl, right side is that complex molecule. So forward reaction: nitro aryl + something -> product (complex). But we need product? The target molecule maybe the product of previous step? Actually earlier precursors were that complex molecule and O=S(=O)(Cl)c1ccccc1F. That product would be sulfonamide linking them. So product SMILES would be CC(C)(C)OC(=O)N1CCN(c2cc(N)cc3c2OC2(CCC2)CC3)CC1S(=O)(=O)c1ccc(F)cc1. That is not the same as the complex molecule alone. So template 2895 seems unrelated to sulfonamide; it's nitro aryl to something else. So maybe the target molecule is different. The question says "to the molecule below" but not provided. Possibly the molecule is the product of template_search-2, which we don't have. However we have mapped_rxn for template 2895, which includes reactants (left) and product (right). The product is the complex molecule (the same as precursor1). So maybe the target molecule is that complex molecule. So applying template 2895 to that molecule (as product) will give precursors: the nitro aryl (left side) and something else? The retro template yields two precursors: the nitro aryl and something else? The right side of retro_smarts_template is O=[N+...]... which is nitro aryl. The left side of retro template is product pattern, which includes [C:7]-[#8:6]-[c:5]1... So the other precursor is maybe a carbonyl? Actually the product pattern includes a phenoxy attached to carbonyl? Wait product pattern includes [C:7]-[#8:6]-[c:5]1... That's a carbon attached to O attached to aromatic. That suggests the product is an aryl ether? The other precursor might be something like a carbonyl? But the retro template only shows one product side? Actually retro_smarts_template: product -> reactants (two). The right side includes O=[N+...]... which is nitro aryl. The left side includes [C:7]-[#8:6]-[c:5]1... which is part of product. The other reactant maybe is something else not shown? Might be missing because template is a transformation of nitro aryl to phenoxy? Hard.

Given limited time, maybe the answer expects the precursors list from applying template 2895 to the target molecule, which likely yields the nitro aryl and something else (maybe a carbonyl).
